summary: Labels owns the product behavior. Use direct server reads for the authenticated RSC page, a cacheable authenticated HTTP GET for browser refresh/filtering, and Server Actions for create/rename. Keep Supabase, row mapping, and persistence private to the capability.

tree.purpose: Explicit trusted server surface for authenticated list/create/rename operations; accepts verified actor identity and returns product types.
RSC-facing read surface; authenticates the request session, then calls the private labels store.
Top-level Server Actions for form mutations; authenticates, validates FormData, invokes labels server behavior, and returns serializable form state.
Browser contract for GET /api/labels, including query-string filtering, refresh, and response decoding.
Optional TanStack Query lifecycle for the labels list; owns query keys, stale time, refetch, and post-mutation invalidation.
Small Client Component that renders the list, filter control, refresh control, and mutation forms; consumes client/query contracts rather than Supabase or server modules.

Private Supabase/Postgres adapter; creates a cookie-scoped client with the verified actor, applies tenant/ownership predicates, validates provider rows, and maps snake_case rows to camelCase product values.
Private schemas for transport commands and selected database rows; names and limits label input.
Authenticated RSC route; calls labels/rsc.ts directly and passes initial labels plus an explicit fetch timestamp to LabelsPanel.
Authenticated browser GET boundary; validates q, calls labels/server.ts, returns JSON with private HTTP caching headers and safe error/status translation.
Route-level unexpected-error UI and reporting boundary for the RSC channel.

flows: Initial render: src/app/(authenticated)/labels/page.tsx -> src/modules/labels/rsc.ts -> verified cookie session plus user-scoped Supabase client -> src/modules/labels/server/labels-store.ts -> SELECT explicit label columns with actor/tenant predicates -> validate LabelRow -> map id/name/created_at to id/name/createdAt -> render LabelsPanel with initialData and initialDataUpdatedAt.

Browser refresh/filter: LabelsPanel -> src/modules/labels/client/queries.ts -> src/modules/labels/client.ts -> GET /api/labels?q=<encoded-filter> -> route-local query validation and authentication -> src/modules/labels/server.ts -> labels-store.ts -> JSON response with Cache-Control: private and an appropriate max-age/ETag -> query cache updates without navigation.

Create: form action -> src/modules/labels/actions.ts -> authenticate current request and authorize label creation -> parse and validate name -> src/modules/labels/server.ts -> labels-store.ts INSERT scoped by actor/tenant -> map returned row -> serializable success/form state -> LabelsPanel invalidates the labels query and calls router.refresh() so both browser and RSC-owned reads converge.

Rename: form action -> src/modules/labels/actions.ts -> authenticate and validate labelId/name -> labels/server.ts -> labels-store.ts UPDATE with actor/tenant predicate and matching using/with-check RLS -> distinguish missing/forbidden/conflict -> return serializable action state -> client invalidates the query and refreshes the RSC segment.

Failure ownership: labels-store.ts maps known provider outcomes to stable capability failures; Route Handler maps them to HTTP status/body; Server Actions map them to field/form state; the RSC error boundary reports unexpected defects once. No private adapter reports or exposes raw Supabase errors.

decisions.choice: All label listing, filtering semantics, create, rename, authorization consequences, row mapping, and failure classification belong to src/modules/labels/.
decisions.rationale: The behavior has one product meaning and lifecycle; routes own composition and transport only.

decisions.choice: Use direct RSC access for the page, Route Handler GET for browser reads, and Server Actions for UI mutations.
decisions.rationale: Next.js recommends direct source reads from Server Components, while Route Handlers provide HTTP GET contracts and Server Actions handle form submissions. [Next.js Route Handlers](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers) [Next.js Backend for Frontend](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/backend-for-frontend) [Next.js Forms](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/forms)

decisions.choice: Authenticate independently at rsc.ts, route.ts, and actions.ts; pass the verified actor explicitly inward.
decisions.rationale: Layouts, middleware, hidden fields, and client state are not authorization. Use a cookie-scoped Supabase client paired with the identity derived from that same session; do not accept caller-supplied actor or tenant values.

decisions.choice: Apply capability permission checks before store calls, and repeat tenant/ownership predicates in Supabase queries and RLS.
decisions.rationale: RLS is defense in depth, not a replacement for capability policy. Keep Supabase clients and service credentials server-only; no alternative provider abstraction is needed.

decisions.choice: Validate unknown HTTP/FormData input once at each channel boundary, validate selected provider rows in labels-store.ts, and map snake_case storage rows to camelCase product values there.
decisions.rationale: Transport contracts and database contracts have separate trust transitions; raw rows never leave the private adapter.

decisions.choice: Use private browser HTTP caching plus a capability-owned browser query cache; do not add a shared server result cache initially.
decisions.rationale: Authenticated results are user-scoped, so shared caching risks data leakage. The GET response can be browser-cacheable with `Cache-Control: private`; TanStack Query owns refresh/filter lifecycle. Mutation success invalidates the browser query and refreshes the RSC view. Next.js GET Route Handlers are not cached by default and require explicit opt-in/configuration. [Next.js Route Handlers](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers)

decisions.choice: Each outer channel translates expected failures into its native contract; unexpected failures are captured once at that channel boundary.
decisions.rationale: RSC needs render/error-boundary behavior, Actions need serializable form state, and HTTP needs status plus safe JSON.

risks: A shared CDN cache must not be enabled for the authenticated GET; retain `private` caching unless the response is redesigned around a non-user-scoped contract.
Concurrent renames require a conflict policy, such as a unique constraint and stable conflict error mapping.
If labels are tenant-owned, every list, insert, and update path must receive the verified tenant identity and enforce it in both SQL predicates and RLS.
If the initial RSC value seeds the browser query, preserve its source timestamp; otherwise the client may treat hydration time as freshness and delay the intended refetch.
